translation_notes: ex = Namespace("http://example.org/") -> `@prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .` placed inside the function body, where the assignment was (block scope): ex.subject/ex.hasPart/ex.Part become ex:subject/ex:hasPart/ex:Part. Legitimate here only because `ex` is not used as a runtime object anywhere else -- @prefix produces no Namespace object.

the two assertion.add() calls merge into one island; `assertion` is a plain local Graph, so the natural `assertion += g{ ... }` works (contrast with the read-only Nanopub.assertion property elsewhere in this file)

IMPORTANT negative finding: the mechanical draft turned BNode("objnode") into the island label _:objnode. That is WRONG here and was reverted. ldpy's _:label is fresh at every evaluation with an rdflib-style 33-character identifier, while BNode("objnode") keeps the label "objnode" -- and nanopub's _replace_blank_nodes() branches on exactly that: `re.match(r'^[Na-zA-Z0-9]{33}$', str(bnode))` decides between a counter-based URI (...#_1) and a label-based one (...#_objnode). Verified: the ldpy label produces N057c...-style ids, so the signed nanopub, its trusty URI and its signature would all have differed. The faithful translation keeps `bnode = BNode("objnode")` in Python and interpolates {bnode} in both term positions. A blank node label is not always opaque scaffolding.

context shim: `from tests.conftest import default_conf, profile_test, skip_if_nanopub_server_unavailable, testsuite, testsuite_conf` replaced by `from nanopub_context import default_conf` -- the upstream conftest fetches a signing key from the online nanopub test suite (network + nanopub_testsuite_connector); the shim rebuilds the same Profile with a locally generated RSA key and copies the NanopubConf fields verbatim. Imported once, so both sides sign with the same key. Identical for both sides.
on the ldpy side Namespace and RDF become dead names in the rdflib import line, which is left untouched (the extract carries the source file's shared preamble)

demo harness added identically to both representations: wraps Nanopub to capture the instance, republishes the four named graphs at module level and PRINTS the trusty source_uri, so the driver's stdout comparison covers the signature and the trusty hash as well as the graphs. default_conf sets both add_*_generated_time to False, so nothing is time-dependent here (unlike the default NanopubConf).
the driver puts the corpus checkout of commit 05022dc4bc (and the example directory) on sys.path; sign() is local crypto, so the region runs entirely offline
